title.narrative: The Yemen International Forum Second Round - 2023

description.narrative: Contract related to: The Yemen International Forum Second Round - 2023 - This 12-months measure will support inclusive and participatory Yemeni-Yemeni dialogue involving participants from all main groups in Yemeni society, notably women, youth, civil society actors, mediators and journalists as well as all political parties. The aim of this dialogue, which will gravitate around the 2023 Yemen International Forum in The Hague, is to facilitate discussions on potential ways forward and on agreements that can assist in avoiding a return to full-scale conflict and thereby mitigate the impact of the conflict on civilians. The action will be implemented in close cooperation with EU Member States which are supporting Yemeni-Yemeni dialogue and it will complement other EU support in the field of mediation and peacebuilding in Yemen.

title.narrative: A gender perspective was mainstreamed throughout the implementation of the intervention.

description.narrative: Obligatory for all crisis response and conflict prevention/peacebuilding/crisispreparedness actions

comment.narrative: Gender was considered from day one with a Sanaa Center gender expert monitoring and informing the process and implementation of the project. Restrictions on movement for women were taken into consideration at the time of planning the travel and when a number of women participants had difficulty getting a visa to travel the Sanaa Center intervened by applying diplomatic pressure to ensure that women participants were allowed to participate. Also making participation of women easy was one of the objectives of shuttle diplomacy by engaging parties controlling travel points to ensure there is no obstruction to the movement of participants. In addition to mainstreaming gender throughout the sessions there was one dedicated livestreamed plenary session on gender entitled Missed opportunities to tackle women exclusion and multifaceted forms of genderbased violence..

title.narrative: Number (%) of members of target groups who consider that their concerns have been or are being addressed

description.narrative: This indicator can be expressed as a number or as a percentage but not as both. In case of use of percentage, an estimated total number of the targeted population group needs to be known.

comment.narrative: The planned target was that minimum 120 members 80 of the participants of YIF II including 30 women consider that their concerns have been addressed during YIF II. The YIF II saw wider participation in terms of political parties. It was also marked with wider participation of groups that that been sidelines from the peace process such as the minorities victims of human rights violations practitioners and specialists civil society tribes private sector local mediators and groups from geographically underrepresented regions such as the Tahama region and Al Mahra governorate. The YIF II tackled a variety of issues which were a priority to the different stakeholder groups participating. The YIF Agenda was carefully designed in consultation with the stakeholder groups to ensure that adequate space was provided to discuss the priorities of the different groups. The project focused on three main themes Political Pathways to peace Economic Recovery and Justice and Reconciliation with other crosscutting themes such as gender equality and womens participation security reform and environment and water. The project was designed as a broader consultative process culminating into a three day conference offering several dialogue and discussion opportunities through plenary sessions parallel sessions side sessions and closed working groups. 98 participants gave a positive reponse about the various sessions that took place at the YIF II conference 98 of the participants of the YIF gave a positive feedback about the YIF II conference agenda 99 gave a positive feedback about the session themes that had been selected And 96 confirmed conduciveness of the YIF conference to open and candid discussions. According to the participants the YIF II conference facilitated all parties interested in the Yemeni issue to meet agree and hope for peace in Yemen. The conference provided comprehensive knowledge and understanding about the conflict dialogue and possible scenarios and the way forward. The topics discussed at the conference provided a fertile background for conducting discussions with other actors and in some ways influenced peoples readiness to recognize the importance of some issues they had not appreciated before and listening to other participants and what these topics mean for them. The conference provided opportunities to meet with political leaders and discuss issues that were the main concern for Yemenis politically and economically and ways to stop the war. It also facilitated discussions with a number of ambassadors and envoys about many topics related to the political and economic aspects and ways of coordination and joint cooperation.

title.narrative: The intervention brought the expected change. Obligatory for IcSP Article 3 and NDICI Crisis Response

description.narrative: The intervention brought the expected change. Obligatory for IcSP Article 3 and NDICI Crisis Response Obligatory for IcSP Article 3 and NDICI Crisis Response

comment.narrative: At the time the project was launched the prolonged nature of the conflict in Yemen had increased hostilities and mutual distrust between Yemeni groups and strained relations on and across the local national and regional levels. Given the polarisation of the political space and lack of trustworthy and safe channels for communication bringing together diverse Yemeni stakeholders and engaging them dialogues for peace in Yemen was very difficult. In 2022 the YIF I had brought together over 200 Yemeni and international peace actors together on one platform and made an attempt to reflect Yemeni voices in the conversation on peace in Yemen.

The expected change was that the conversation on peace in Yemen is enhanced grounded in local knowledge and realities and reflective of the voices of the different groups in Yemen. A lot of information was generated through the various discussions that took place in the YIF. The outcomes also reflected the voices of various groups in Yemen. Marginalised groups such as the Bahais Yemeni Jews Muhammasheen women who had not been represented before participated in the YIF II. Groups from marginalised regions such as the Tahama region and Al Mahrah also participated.

comment.narrative: At the time the project was launched the prolonged nature of the conflict in Yemen had increased hostilities and mutual distrust between Yemeni groups and strained relations on and across the local national and regional levels. Given the polarisation of the political space and lack of trustworthy and safe channels for communication the possibility of reaching a sustainable agreement was remote.

Yes. Groups having different views participated in the YIF II and were engaged in dialogues on different topics. The scenario building activity brought all these diverse actors together to work collectively to identify key conflict drivers and build the possible future scenarios for Yemen. In her closing speech Rana Ghanem Assistant Secretary General of the Nasserites party in Yemen said that The very important topics that were discussed during the forum reiterated and stressed the importance of continued dialogues between the political social and local entities. Because of the importance of these kind of dialogues in bridging the gaps between us and helping us to reach agreements and solutions that will alleviate the suffering and differences and help us build a common future. After 8 years of war we have come to believe that there can be no victor from violence and the only way we Yemeni can end this is by going back to the negotiating table. Implementing the recommendations of this forum and planning for the future is our responsibility. We hope this forum continues to be an open platform for dialogue and discussion and to produce valuable outcomes.

100 achieved Yes the project contributed to a multilateral approach to conflict prevention peacebuilding and stabilisation in the given context of Yemen. As part of the Yemen International Forum II YIF II the Sanaa Center and its partners held a series of meetings discussing the importance of transitional justice within peace efforts and exploring avenues for enhanced cooperation on the topic between Yemeni civil society organizations local political actors and the international community. description.narrative: Public perception of the effectiveness of the peace process

comment.narrative: Since the National Dialogue Conference in 2013 this is the first and only platform that gathers this number of Yemenis from different political economic and social backgrounds to work towards ending the current deadlock and craft a new future for Yemen postsettlement. Such dialogue has never been more vital. If a SaudiHouthi agreement is indeed imminent and Yemen inches towards a political settlement the input on what peace will look like from Yemens broader political and civil actors will be key if wanting genuine and sustainable peace. The YIF is a first step towards this dialogue. In addition to complimenting the UNled peace process and Track II initiatives this YemeniYemeni dialogue serves to guide and inform current and future discourse and outcomes on Yemens path towards peace. Important breakthroughs were achieved at the Hague this year with wider engagement from the political groups a declaration for transitional justice endorsed by Yemens civil society organizations and the international community and constructive ongoing dialogue between bankers and economic experts on how to deescalate Yemens economic warfare. 99 of the participants had a positive perception of the YIF II conference which was designed to completed the UNled peace process. Moreover the willingness of such a diverse set of actors to participate in the YIF and engage in a dialogue for peace is a testament to improved public perception of the effectiveness and fairness of the peace process.
